views.name: band_blocks_base
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  "block_height" AS block_height,
  TRY_TO_TIMESTAMP_NTZ("block_timestamp") AS block_timestamp_ts,
  "block_timestamp_truncated" AS block_timestamp_truncated,
  "block_hash" AS block_hash,
  "proposer_address" AS proposer_address,
  "last_commit_hash" AS last_commit_hash,
  "data_hash" AS data_hash,
  "validators_hash" AS validators_hash,
  "next_validators_hash" AS next_validators_hash,
  "consensus_hash" AS consensus_hash,
  "app_hash" AS app_hash,
  "last_results_hash" AS last_results_hash,
  "evidence_hash" AS evidence_hash,
  "signatures" AS signatures_variant
FROM CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.BLOCKS

params.description: One-row-per-block facts for BandChain blocks: block identifiers, timestamps, hashes, proposer, and signature variant stored as a normalized base view.
params.when_to_use: Get block-level metadata (timestamp, hashes, proposer) for a given block height or time range. | Join block-level context to transactions, messages, or oracle requests when you need one row per block. | Compute block-level aggregates (counts of blocks, time-range statistics) or derive rates/latencies per block. | Filter or partition downstream analyses by block_timestamp_truncated (e.g., hourly/daily) or by proposer_address.
params.output_schema: block_height: Block height (integer) — derived from source column CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.BLOCKS.block_height. Grain: one row per block_height. | block_timestamp_ts: Block timestamp as a Snowflake TIMESTAMP_NTZ (TRY_TO_TIMESTAMP_NTZ applied) — derived from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.BLOCKS.block_timestamp. | block_timestamp_truncated: Block timestamp already truncated in source (likely to a coarser unit such as hour/day) — derived from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.BLOCKS.block_timestamp_truncated. | block_hash: Block hash (hex/string) — derived from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.BLOCKS.block_hash. | proposer_address: Address of the block proposer (string) — derived from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.BLOCKS.proposer_address. | last_commit_hash: Last commit hash (string) — derived from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.BLOCKS.last_commit_hash. | data_hash: Data hash (string) — derived from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.BLOCKS.data_hash. | validators_hash: Validators hash (string) — derived from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.BLOCKS.validators_hash. | next_validators_hash: Next validators hash (string) — derived from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.BLOCKS.next_validators_hash. | consensus_hash: Consensus parameters hash (string) — derived from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.BLOCKS.consensus_hash. | app_hash: Application state hash after block (string) — derived from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.BLOCKS.app_hash. | last_results_hash: Last results hash (string) — derived from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.BLOCKS.last_results_hash. | evidence_hash: Evidence hash (string) — derived from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.BLOCKS.evidence_hash. | signatures_variant: Signatures payload/variant field (renamed to signatures_variant) — derived from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.BLOCKS.signatures.
params.grounded_columns: CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.BLOCKS.block_height | CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.BLOCKS.block_timestamp | CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.BLOCKS.block_timestamp_truncated | CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.BLOCKS.block_hash | CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.BLOCKS.proposer_address | CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.BLOCKS.last_commit_hash | CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.BLOCKS.data_hash | CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.BLOCKS.validators_hash | CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.BLOCKS.next_validators_hash | CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.BLOCKS.consensus_hash | CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.BLOCKS.app_hash | CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.BLOCKS.last_results_hash | CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.BLOCKS.evidence_hash | CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.BLOCKS.signatures
params.metric: block_count = COUNT(block_height)  -- count of blocks (safe to aggregate over this view's rows) | distinct_proposers = COUNT(DISTINCT proposer_address)  -- number of unique proposers in the selected block set | time_range_min = MIN(block_timestamp_ts)  -- earliest block timestamp in the selected block set | time_range_max = MAX(block_timestamp_ts)  -- latest block timestamp in the selected block set
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to per-validator or per-proposer dimension (e.g., a proposer metadata table keyed by proposer_address) on proposer_address — safe because this view is one row per block_height and proposer_address is at most one value per block, so joining to a 1:1 proposer dimension will not duplicate block rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to time-based dimensions keyed by block_timestamp_truncated (e.g., calendar/hour/day dimension) on block_timestamp_truncated — safe because block_timestamp_truncated is a single value per block row. | DO NOT directly join this view to one-to-many event/detail tables (for example: band_transactions_base or band_messages_variant_expanded) without aggregation on the many-side first — those sibling tables typically have multiple transactions/messages per block_height, so a naive join will multiply block-level rows and any aggregates computed on this view. | If you must combine with a one-to-many child (transactions/messages/requests) to compute block-level metrics, either: a) aggregate the child to one row per block_height first (e.g., COUNT(*) AS tx_count GROUP BY block_height) then join on block_height, or b) join and then GROUP BY block_height in the final query so measures from this view remain correct. | Joins on block_height are the canonical key to combine block-level facts with block-scoped aggregates from sibling views (e.g., join to band_transactions_base ON block_height AFTER aggregating transactions to block_height if needed). | Joining to sibling normalized block-level views is safe (one-to-one) if they also declare one row per block_height; verify sibling view grain before joining to avoid accidental duplication.

views.description: Normalized projection of CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.BLOCKS with canonical column names and numeric timestamp. Useful as a clean block-level source for joins, time-series, and aggregations. | Use for: block-level timelines; join blocks to band transactions/messages/events; proposer or validator analysis

views.name: band_transactions_base
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  "txhash" AS txhash,
  "block_height" AS block_height,
  TRY_TO_TIMESTAMP_NTZ("block_timestamp") AS block_timestamp_ts,
  "block_timestamp_truncated" AS block_timestamp_truncated,
  "transaction_type" AS transaction_type,
  "gas_wanted" AS gas_wanted,
  "gas_used" AS gas_used,
  "sender" AS sender,
  "fee" AS fee_variant,
  "memo" AS memo
FROM CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.TRANSACTIONS

params.description: Provides one-row-per-transaction facts for Band chain transactions (transaction-level metadata, gas, fee, sender, timestamps and memo).
params.when_to_use: List or filter transactions by hash, sender, block height, timestamp, transaction type, gas or memo. | Compute transaction-level aggregates (counts, distinct txhashes) or time-series of transaction counts/volumes when grouped by block_timestamp_truncated or block_height. | Join transaction-level attributes onto other per-transaction datasets (messages, oracle requests) when those datasets are aggregated to transaction granularity first. | Drive dashboards showing recent transactions, per-block transaction counts, gas usage distribution per transaction, or fee variants per transaction.
params.output_schema: txhash: unique transaction identifier (derived from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.TRANSACTIONS.txhash). This is the natural primary key for the view (one row per txhash). | block_height: block height containing the transaction (derived from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.TRANSACTIONS.block_height). | block_timestamp_ts: full timestamp as a TIMESTAMP_NTZ (derived from TRY_TO_TIMESTAMP_NTZ(CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.TRANSACTIONS.block_timestamp)). | block_timestamp_truncated: block timestamp truncated to a time grain (derived from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.TRANSACTIONS.block_timestamp_truncated). Use this for time-binning as provided by the source. | transaction_type: textual transaction type/category (derived from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.TRANSACTIONS.transaction_type). | gas_wanted: gas wanted/limit for the transaction (derived from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.TRANSACTIONS.gas_wanted). | gas_used: gas actually used by the transaction (derived from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.TRANSACTIONS.gas_used). | sender: transaction signer/sender address (derived from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.TRANSACTIONS.sender). | fee_variant: raw fee value/structure as provided (derived from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.TRANSACTIONS.fee). The view exposes it under the name fee_variant. | memo: transaction memo field (derived from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.TRANSACTIONS.memo).
params.metric: tx_count = COUNT(txhash)  -- count of transactions (use DISTINCT txhash if combining with joins that may duplicate rows) | distinct_senders = COUNT(DISTINCT sender)  -- number of unique senders in the selected set | sum_gas_wanted = SUM(gas_wanted)  -- total gas_wanted across rows | sum_gas_used = SUM(gas_used)  -- total gas_used across rows
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to band_blocks_base on band_transactions_base.block_height = band_blocks_base.block_height — safe because band_blocks_base is one-row-per-block and band_transactions_base is one-row-per-transaction; joining block attributes onto transactions will NOT duplicate transaction-level measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to band_oracle_requests_base only after aggregating oracle requests to transaction granularity (e.g., group oracle requests by txhash). Do NOT join raw oracle requests (which are likely one-to-many per txhash) directly to this view if you intend to SUM or COUNT transactions, because that will multiply transaction rows and duplicate measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to band_messages_variant_expanded only after reducing messages to one row per txhash (for example, aggregate or pick a representative message per txhash). band_messages_variant_expanded is a reshape of messages and is typically one-to-many per transaction; direct joins will duplicate transaction rows. | do NOT join directly to any one-to-many child tables/views (e.g., message-level or input/output exploded views such as bitcoin_inputs_address_exploded or bitcoin_outputs_address_exploded) without first aggregating those children to txhash level. Direct joins to one-to-many siblings will multiply transaction-level counts and sums. | If you need transaction-level measures (sums/averages) after joining to one-to-many detail, perform aggregation on the joined result and aggregate back to txhash (or the desired grain), or pre-aggregate the one-to-many side and then join on txhash to preserve correct cardinality. | When joining on txhash, prefer equality on txhash because band_transactions_base has exactly one row per txhash (its declared grain). If joining to another view that is also one-row-per-txhash (after any required reshaping/aggregation), the join is safe for measures on either side.

views.description: Clean projection of CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.TRANSACTIONS exposing canonical transaction identifiers, sender and gas metrics and preserving fee VARIANT for downstream normalization. | Use for: transaction counts and gas consumption; fee analysis after normalizing fee_variant; join transactions to messages/logs

views.name: band_messages_variant_expanded
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  mtx.txhash AS txhash,
  TRY_TO_TIMESTAMP_NTZ(mtx.block_timestamp) AS block_timestamp_ts,
  mtx.block_height AS block_height,
  f.key AS message_field,
  f.value AS message_variant
FROM (
  SELECT
    "txhash" AS txhash,
    "block_timestamp" AS block_timestamp,
    "block_height" AS block_height,
    OBJECT_CONSTRUCT_KEEP_NULL(
      'oracle_Activate', "oracle_Activate",
      'oracle_AddReporter', "oracle_AddReporter",
      'oracle_CreateDataSource', "oracle_CreateDataSource",
      'oracle_CreateOracleScript', "oracle_CreateOracleScript",
      'oracle_EditDataSource', "oracle_EditDataSource",
      'oracle_EditOracleScript', "oracle_EditOracleScript",
      'oracle_Report', "oracle_Report",
      'oracle_Request', "oracle_Request",
      'oracle_RemoveReporter', "oracle_RemoveReporter",
      'cosmos_sdk_MsgDelegate', "cosmos_sdk_MsgDelegate",
      'cosmos_sdk_MsgEditValidator', "cosmos_sdk_MsgEditValidator",
      'cosmos_sdk_MsgMultiSend', "cosmos_sdk_MsgMultiSend",
      'cosmos_sdk_MsgSend', "cosmos_sdk_MsgSend",
      'cosmos_sdk_MsgBeginRedelegate', "cosmos_sdk_MsgBeginRedelegate",
      'cosmos_sdk_MsgCreateValidator', "cosmos_sdk_MsgCreateValidator",
      'cosmos_sdk_MsgDeposit', "cosmos_sdk_MsgDeposit",
      'cosmos_sdk_MsgFundCommunityPool', "cosmos_sdk_MsgFundCommunityPool",
      'cosmos_sdk_MsgModifyWithdrawAddress', "cosmos_sdk_MsgModifyWithdrawAddress",
      'cosmos_sdk_MsgSubmitEvidence', "cosmos_sdk_MsgSubmitEvidence",
      'cosmos_sdk_MsgSubmitProposal', "cosmos_sdk_MsgSubmitProposal",
      'cosmos_sdk_MsgUndelegate', "cosmos_sdk_MsgUndelegate",
      'cosmos_sdk_MsgUnjail', "cosmos_sdk_MsgUnjail",
      'cosmos_sdk_MsgVerifyInvariant', "cosmos_sdk_MsgVerifyInvariant",
      'cosmos_sdk_MsgVote', "cosmos_sdk_MsgVote",
      'cosmos_sdk_MsgWithdrawDelegationReward', "cosmos_sdk_MsgWithdrawDelegationReward",
      'cosmos_sdk_MsgWithdrawValidatorCommission', "cosmos_sdk_MsgWithdrawValidatorCommission"
    ) AS msg_map
  FROM CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.MESSAGES
) mtx,
LATERAL FLATTEN(INPUT => mtx.msg_map) f
WHERE f.value IS NOT NULL
grain: one row per txhash + message_field (for non-null message VARIANTs)

params.description: Explodes VARIANT message object fields for Band transactions so each row represents one txhash + message_field (only for non-null variant entries). Useful for analyzing message types and their raw contents per transaction.
params.when_to_use: Count or list distinct message fields or message variants per transaction (e.g., how many transactions contain a given message_field). | Filter transactions by a specific message_field or inspect the raw VARIANT payload for a message key. | Compose higher-level aggregates per transaction (e.g., number of message fields per tx) by grouping this view's rows. | Join with transaction- or block-level views when you need message-level detail alongside transaction metadata.
params.output_schema: txhash: transaction hash for the originating transaction — derived from the inner SELECT column "txhash" (alias mtx.txhash in outer query). | block_timestamp_ts: block timestamp converted to TIMESTAMP_NTZ — derived from TRY_TO_TIMESTAMP_NTZ(mtx.block_timestamp), where mtx.block_timestamp comes from the inner SELECT column "block_timestamp". | block_height: block height of the transaction — derived from the inner SELECT column "block_height" (mtx.block_height). | message_field: key/name of the VARIANT object field extracted by f.key from OBJECT_CONSTRUCT_KEEP_NULL result. | message_variant: VARIANT value (raw message content) for the corresponding message_field — extracted as f.value from OBJECT_CONSTRUCT_KEEP_NULL result.
params.grounded_columns: txhash | block_timestamp | block_height | oracle_Activate | oracle_AddReporter | oracle_CreateDataSource | oracle_CreateOracleScript | oracle_EditDataSource | oracle_EditOracleScript | oracle_Report | oracle_Request | oracle_RemoveReporter | cosmos_sdk_MsgDelegate | cosmos_sdk_MsgEditValidator | cosmos_sdk_MsgMultiSend | cosmos_sdk_MsgSend | cosmos_sdk_MsgBeginRedelegate | cosmos_sdk_MsgCreateValidator | cosmos_sdk_MsgDeposit | cosmos_sdk_MsgFundCommunityPool | cosmos_sdk_MsgModifyWithdrawAddress
params.metric: row = 1  -- the view is a reshaped, row-level expansion: one output row represents one (txhash, message_field) combination when message VARIANT entries exist. | message_count_per_tx = COUNT(message_field) per txhash  -- can be computed by grouping this view by txhash (this view provides one row per message_field so COUNT(message_field) yields number of message fields present for that tx). | distinct_message_fields = COUNT(DISTINCT message_field) per grouping  -- derived by standard aggregation over message_field.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to band_transactions_base on txhash — safe because this view is one row per txhash+message_field (transaction-level columns like block_height/timestamp are constant per txhash). Joining to a one-row-per-tx table on txhash will not duplicate message-level rows; it simply enriches each message row with transaction-level attributes. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to band_blocks_base on block_height OR block_timestamp_ts (block key) — safe if band_blocks_base is one row per block_height (or per block_timestamp). Joining on block_height will not duplicate these view rows because this view already has at most one block reference per row. | DO NOT join without care to one-to-many views/tables (e.g., ethereum_token_transfers_base, bitcoin_inputs_address_exploded, bitcoin_outputs_address_exploded, or any other table that is one-to-many relative to txhash) directly on txhash or a non-unique key, unless you first aggregate this view or the other side. Such joins will multiply this view's message-level rows and thereby incorrectly inflate counts/metrics — for example, joining directly to a token_transfers table (many transfers per tx) would produce row-multiplication equal to transfers_per_tx * message_fields_per_tx. | If you need to combine with a one-to-many table, choose one of two safe patterns: (a) aggregate the one-to-many side to one row per txhash (or per block) before joining, or (b) aggregate this view to a single-row-per-txhash metric (e.g., message_count_per_tx) before joining. Both preserve correct cardinality for derived metrics. | When composing measures: treat each row here as atomic (row = one message field instance). Any SUM/COUNT over message_variant or message_field should be computed at this grain or after explicit aggregation that documents the expected cardinality.

views.description: Unpivoted/expanded view of CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.MESSAGES that turns the many oracle_/cosmos_sdk_ VARIANT columns into one row per message-type-field present. Useful to search/aggregate on specific message payloads and to join messages by txhash and message_type. | Use for: find all messages of a given oracle_ or cosmos_sdk_ type; extract fields from message_variant for payload analysis; join message payloads to transactions/logs

views.name: bitcoin_outputs_address_exploded
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  "transaction_hash" AS transaction_hash,
  "block_hash" AS block_hash,
  "block_number" AS block_number,
  "block_timestamp" AS block_timestamp,
  "index" AS output_index,
  f.value::STRING AS address,
  "value" AS value
FROM CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BITCOIN.OUTPUTS,
LATERAL FLATTEN(INPUT => "addresses") f
grain: one row per output (transaction_hash + output_index) + address

params.description: Rows of Bitcoin transaction outputs exploded by each address receiving the output (one row per transaction_hash + output_index + address), providing block and value context for each output-address pair.
params.when_to_use: List all outputs (with value and block info) paid to each address; e.g., "Which outputs were sent to this address?" | Aggregate received value per address or per block by composing/grouping this view (e.g., total BTC received by address over time). | Join to transaction- or block-level views to enrich outputs with transaction or block attributes (while preserving correct cardinality when done as described). | Filter outputs by block range, timestamp, transaction hash, output index, or address for downstream analysis or joins.
params.output_schema: transaction_hash: transaction identifier for the output; derived from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BITCOIN.OUTPUTS."transaction_hash" | block_hash: block identifier containing the transaction; derived from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BITCOIN.OUTPUTS."block_hash" | block_number: block height containing the transaction; derived from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BITCOIN.OUTPUTS."block_number" | block_timestamp: block timestamp for the transaction; derived from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BITCOIN.OUTPUTS."block_timestamp" | output_index: index of the output within the transaction (renamed from "index"); derived from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BITCOIN.OUTPUTS."index" | address: a single address that is a recipient of this output, produced by flattening the OUTPUTS.addresses array; derived from the lateral flatten alias f.value cast to STRING which reads CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BITCOIN.OUTPUTS."addresses" | value: numeric value of the output (units and type as stored in the base table); derived from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BITCOIN.OUTPUTS."value"
params.metric: value = CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BITCOIN.OUTPUTS.value  -- per-row measure: the output value for this transaction_hash + output_index + address row | count_outputs = COUNT(*)  -- when aggregated after grouping, counts exploded output-address rows (one per output-address pair) | sum_value = SUM(value)  -- when aggregated, yields total value across the grouped exploded rows (e.g., total received by an address)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a transaction- or block-level one-row-per-transaction/one-row-per-block view on transaction_hash or block_hash respectively — safe because this view is one-row-per-output-address and joining to a one-row-per-transaction or one-row-per-block dimension will not duplicate rows and thus will not multiply value measures. Example: JOIN band_transactions_base ON bitcoin_outputs_address_exploded.transaction_hash = band_transactions_base.transaction_hash | safe: join to band_blocks_base ON bitcoin_outputs_address_exploded.block_hash = band_blocks_base.block_hash (block-level attributes added per output-address row without duplicating measures) because band_blocks_base is one row per block. | UNSAFE without re-aggregation: do NOT join directly to another one-to-many detail that expands per transaction into multiple rows (for example, a view that is one-row-per-input or one-row-per-message for the same transaction) without first aggregating either side. Joining to such one-to-many tables will multiply bitcoin_outputs_address_exploded.value and row counts. Example to avoid: directly joining bitcoin_inputs_address_exploded (one-row-per-input-address) on transaction_hash will create a cross-product between inputs and outputs for the same transaction if there are multiple inputs/outputs. | If you need data from another one-to-many view (e.g., bitcoin_inputs_address_exploded), aggregate that other view to one row per transaction (or per join key) before joining. For example: derive inputs_summary AS (SELECT transaction_hash, SUM(value) AS total_input_value FROM bitcoin_inputs_address_exploded GROUP BY transaction_hash) and then JOIN inputs_summary ON transaction_hash — this preserves correct measures. | When joining to address-level dimensions keyed by address (if such a dimension is one-row-per-address), it is safe to JOIN on address because this view is one-row-per-output-address (each output-address row will get the address attributes once and measures are not duplicated). | When composing higher-level metrics (e.g., total received by address), perform aggregation on this view (GROUP BY address) rather than relying on joins that might replicate rows.

views.description: Explode CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BITCOIN.OUTPUTS 'addresses' VARIANT (array) into one row per output-address. Keeps transaction and block references and value for address-level UTXO analysis. | Use for: address balance approximations from outputs; UTXO-level analyses by address; join outputs to inputs via spent_transaction_hash/spent_output_index or address

views.name: bitcoin_inputs_address_exploded
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  "transaction_hash" AS transaction_hash,
  "block_hash" AS block_hash,
  "block_number" AS block_number,
  "block_timestamp" AS block_timestamp,
  "index" AS input_index,
  f.value::STRING AS address,
  "value" AS value,
  "spent_transaction_hash" AS spent_transaction_hash,
  "spent_output_index" AS spent_output_index
FROM CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BITCOIN.INPUTS,
LATERAL FLATTEN(INPUT => "addresses") f
grain: one row per input (transaction_hash + input_index) + address

params.description: Provides one row per Bitcoin transaction input address (transaction_hash + input_index + address), exposing input-level metadata and spending info.
params.when_to_use: List all input addresses for Bitcoin transactions and their input-level values and spending targets. | Compute totals or aggregates of input value by address, transaction, block, or time interval (must aggregate after using this view). | Join inputs to exploded outputs (or transactions/blocks) to analyze UTXO flows, address reuse, or input/output matching when careful about cardinality. | Identify which input came from which address and whether that input output has been spent (spent_transaction_hash/spent_output_index).
params.output_schema: transaction_hash: the transaction hash for the input; derived from INPUTS."transaction_hash" in the source table. | block_hash: the block hash containing the transaction; derived from INPUTS."block_hash". | block_number: the block height/number containing the transaction; derived from INPUTS."block_number". | block_timestamp: timestamp of the block containing the transaction; derived from INPUTS."block_timestamp". | input_index: index of the input within the transaction; derived from INPUTS."index". | address: one address for this input (exploded from the addresses array); derived from the lateral flatten alias f.value cast to STRING (originally from INPUTS."addresses"). | value: numeric value (satoshi or native unit as in source) associated with the input; derived from INPUTS."value". | spent_transaction_hash: the transaction hash that spends the referenced output (if present); derived from INPUTS."spent_transaction_hash". | spent_output_index: the output index in the spending transaction that consumes this input's referenced output (if present); derived from INPUTS."spent_output_index".
params.metric: value = SUM(value)  -- when aggregating input monetary amount, sum the 'value' column across the grouping you need (e.g., BY address, BY transaction_hash, BY block_number). | count_inputs = COUNT(*)  -- counts exploded input-address rows; use to count input-address occurrences. | distinct_inputs = COUNT(DISTINCT transaction_hash || '::' || input_index)  -- counts distinct (transaction_hash, input_index) pairs when needed to avoid double-counting exploded addresses.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a transaction-level or block-level dimension (e.g., band_transactions_base or band_blocks_base) on transaction_hash or block_hash/block_number respectively — safe because this view is one row per input-address, and joining to a one-row-per-transaction or one-row-per-block dimension will not duplicate input rows. | Safe join example: JOIN band_transactions_base t ON bitcoin_inputs_address_exploded.transaction_hash = t.transaction_hash — safe because band_transactions_base is normalized to one row per transaction (does not multiply input rows). | Do NOT naive-join to any outputs or other exploded/one-to-many views (for example, bitcoin_outputs_address_exploded) without re-aggregation or explicit deduplication first, because those are one-to-many relative to transactions and will multiply rows and sum-measures. If you need to combine with bitcoin_outputs_address_exploded, join on (transaction_hash, output_index) with outputs de-duplicated to the same grain or aggregate both sides to a common grain (e.g., per transaction or per address) before joining. | Do NOT join this view to other exploded address views (one-to-many on the same transaction) expecting measures to remain unchanged; instead either: a) aggregate this view to the desired grain (e.g., GROUP BY transaction_hash or address) before joining, or b) join on keys that are 1:1 (e.g., full input identifier) and ensure the other side is also 1:1 on that key. | To preserve correct sums when composing: if you join to a table that is N rows per input (N>1), either (1) aggregate that other table to one-row-per-(transaction_hash,input_index,address) first, or (2) aggregate this view to the join grain (e.g., per transaction_hash or per address) before joining. Use distinct_inputs metric if you need to count unique inputs after joins that may multiply rows.

views.description: Explode CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BITCOIN.INPUTS 'addresses' VARIANT into one row per input-address preserving spent transaction pointers for UTXO lineage. | Use for: trace UTXO spending (join inputs to outputs); address-level input volume over time; identify change outputs by address patterns

views.name: ethereum_transactions_base
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  "hash" AS txhash,
  "nonce" AS nonce,
  "transaction_index" AS transaction_index,
  "from_address" AS from_address,
  "to_address" AS to_address,
  "value" AS value,
  "gas" AS gas,
  "gas_price" AS gas_price,
  TRY_TO_TIMESTAMP_NTZ(TO_VARCHAR("block_timestamp")) AS block_timestamp_ts,
  "block_number" AS block_number,
  "block_hash" AS block_hash,
  "receipt_gas_used" AS receipt_gas_used,
  "receipt_contract_address" AS receipt_contract_address,
  "receipt_status" AS receipt_status,
  "receipt_effective_gas_price" AS receipt_effective_gas_price
FROM CRYPTO.CRYPTO_ETHEREUM.TRANSACTIONS

params.description: One-row-per-Ethereum-transaction base view exposing transaction identifiers, parties, value/gas fields, block/time, and receipt outcome fields for analytical composition.
params.when_to_use: Retrieve or filter individual Ethereum transactions by hash, block, sender/recipient, or time. | Compute aggregates over transactions (counts, sum(value), sum(gas), avg(gas_price)) after grouping by block, address, or time. | Join transactions to blocks, token transfers, contracts, or addresses when building higher-level metrics (e.g., per-block throughput, per-address spending) provided joins preserve cardinality or re-aggregate appropriately. | Serve as the base fact for composing receipts-level success/failure rates or gas usage per transaction.
params.output_schema: txhash: transaction hash (derived from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_ETHEREUM.TRANSACTIONS."hash"); unique identifier for the transaction (grain: one row per txhash). | nonce: sender nonce for this transaction (derived from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_ETHEREUM.TRANSACTIONS."nonce"). | transaction_index: index of this transaction within the block (derived from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_ETHEREUM.TRANSACTIONS."transaction_index"). | from_address: sender address of the transaction (derived from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_ETHEREUM.TRANSACTIONS."from_address"). | to_address: recipient address of the transaction (derived from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_ETHEREUM.TRANSACTIONS."to_address"). | value: value transferred by the transaction, in the chain's native unit (derived from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_ETHEREUM.TRANSACTIONS."value"). | gas: gas limit specified by the transaction (derived from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_ETHEREUM.TRANSACTIONS."gas"). | gas_price: legacy gas_price field (derived from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_ETHEREUM.TRANSACTIONS."gas_price"). | block_timestamp_ts: block timestamp converted to timestamp NTZ (derived from TRY_TO_TIMESTAMP_NTZ(TO_VARCHAR(CRYPTO.CRYPTO_ETHEREUM.TRANSACTIONS."block_timestamp"))). | block_number: number of the block containing the transaction (derived from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_ETHEREUM.TRANSACTIONS."block_number"). | block_hash: hash of the block containing the transaction (derived from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_ETHEREUM.TRANSACTIONS."block_hash"). | receipt_gas_used: actual gas used by the transaction as recorded in its receipt (derived from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_ETHEREUM.TRANSACTIONS."receipt_gas_used"). | receipt_contract_address: contract address created by the transaction receipt, if any (derived from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_ETHEREUM.TRANSACTIONS."receipt_contract_address"). | receipt_status: receipt execution status (e.g., success/failure) as recorded in the receipt (derived from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_ETHEREUM.TRANSACTIONS."receipt_status"). | receipt_effective_gas_price: effective gas price applied (EIP-1559) from the receipt (derived from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_ETHEREUM.TRANSACTIONS."receipt_effective_gas_price").
params.metric: tx_count = COUNT(txhash) -- count of transactions (aggregate over txhash). | sum_value = SUM(value) -- total native-chain value transferred by the set of transactions. | sum_gas = SUM(gas) -- total gas limits declared by transactions (note: limit, not used). | sum_receipt_gas_used = SUM(receipt_gas_used) -- total gas actually consumed according to receipts. | avg_gas_price = AVG(gas_price) -- average legacy gas_price across transactions (NULL when not set). | avg_effective_gas_price = AVG(receipt_effective_gas_price) -- average effective gas price from receipts. | success_rate = SUM(CASE WHEN receipt_status IS NOT NULL AND receipt_status <> 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(COUNT(txhash),0) -- fraction of transactions with successful/non-zero receipt_status when receipt_status semantics encode success as non-zero (validate semantics in source).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE: join to a blocks dimension/view on block_number or block_hash (e.g., blocks view keyed by block_number or block_hash) — safe because this view has at most one row per txhash and block key is many transactions to one block (many-to-one from this view to blocks), so joining to block attributes will not duplicate transaction-level measures. | cardinality-SAFE: join to ethereum_contracts_latest on receipt_contract_address = contract_address — safe when ethereum_contracts_latest is one-row-per-contract-address, because each transaction's receipt_contract_address maps to at most one contract record and will not multiply transaction measures. | cardinality-UNSAFE: do NOT directly join to ethereum_token_transfers_base or any token transfers/outputs/inputs exploded reshaped tables (e.g., ethereum_token_transfers_base, bitcoin_outputs_address_exploded, bitcoin_inputs_address_exploded, band_messages_variant_expanded) without aggregation, because they are one-to-many relative to transactions (a single txhash can have zero, one, or many token transfer or input/output rows). Joining these will duplicate transaction-level measures (value, receipt_gas_used) unless you first aggregate the many-side to one row per txhash (for example SUM(amount) GROUP BY txhash) or use analytic/exists patterns that avoid multiplicative effects. | cardinality-UNSAFE: do NOT join to sibling transactions-like views that are also one-row-per-transaction using non-unique keys (e.g., joining ethereum_transactions_base to another transactions view on non-unique fields) unless the join key is txhash; joining on from_address or block_number could create many-to-many multiplicative joins and duplicate aggregates. | safe-join-patterns: to compute per-transaction enriched metrics with token totals, first aggregate token transfers: (SELECT txhash, SUM(amount) AS token_amount FROM ethereum_token_transfers_base GROUP BY txhash) and then LEFT JOIN that single-row-per-txhash result to ethereum_transactions_base on txhash — this preserves transaction-level cardinality. | safe-join-patterns: to compute per-address aggregates, aggregate transactions after join (e.g., GROUP BY from_address with SUM(value), COUNT(txhash)) rather than joining transactions to multi-row address tables that would multiply rows. | note-on-null-keys: when joining on receipt_contract_address or to_address/from_address, be mindful that NULL values may exist; prefer explicit NULL-handling (e.g., COALESCE or join predicates that exclude NULL) if matching semantics require it.

views.description: Normalized projection of CRYPTO.CRYPTO_ETHEREUM.TRANSACTIONS with canonical columns and preserved receipt/gas metrics. Ready for join to logs/traces/contracts. | Use for: gas usage and fee calculations; joins to logs/traces/token_transfers/contracts; transaction success/failure rates

views.name: ethereum_token_transfers_base
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  "transaction_hash" AS transaction_hash,
  "log_index" AS log_index,
  "token_address" AS token_address,
  "from_address" AS from_address,
  "to_address" AS to_address,
  "value" AS value,
  TRY_TO_TIMESTAMP_NTZ(TO_VARCHAR("block_timestamp")) AS block_timestamp_ts,
  "block_number" AS block_number,
  "block_hash" AS block_hash
FROM CRYPTO.CRYPTO_ETHEREUM.TOKEN_TRANSFERS
grain: one row per token transfer (transaction_hash + log_index)

params.description: Provides one row per ERC-20/erc-721 token transfer event on Ethereum, with transfer identifiers, addresses, value, and block metadata.
params.when_to_use: Listing token transfers for transactions or blocks (e.g., show transfers in a given transaction or block range). | Composing token-transfer-level metrics such as counts of transfers, sum of transferred values (after appropriate unit handling), unique token holders movement, or joins to transaction/block dimension views. | Filtering or slicing token transfers by token_address, from_address, to_address, block_number, or block_timestamp_ts for downstream analysis or further aggregation. | Joining transfers to transactions, blocks, or contract metadata when you need transfer-level detail as the grain.
params.output_schema: transaction_hash: transaction identifier (derived from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_ETHEREUM.TOKEN_TRANSFERS.transaction_hash). Uniquely identifies the transaction containing the transfer; part of the view's row grain. | log_index: log index within the transaction (derived from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_ETHEREUM.TOKEN_TRANSFERS.log_index). Combined with transaction_hash forms the unique row key (one row per transfer). | token_address: token contract address involved in the transfer (derived from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_ETHEREUM.TOKEN_TRANSFERS.token_address). | from_address: origin address of the token transfer (derived from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_ETHEREUM.TOKEN_TRANSFERS.from_address). | to_address: destination address of the token transfer (derived from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_ETHEREUM.TOKEN_TRANSFERS.to_address). | value: raw transfer value as stored (derived from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_ETHEREUM.TOKEN_TRANSFERS.value). This is the on-chain numeric amount in the token's smallest unit; token-specific decimals are NOT applied here. | block_timestamp_ts: block timestamp converted to a TIMESTAMP/NTZ (derived from TRY_TO_TIMESTAMP_NTZ(TO_VARCHAR(CRYPTO.CRYPTO_ETHEREUM.TOKEN_TRANSFERS.block_timestamp))). | block_number: block number containing the transfer (derived from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_ETHEREUM.TOKEN_TRANSFERS.block_number). | block_hash: block hash containing the transfer (derived from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_ETHEREUM.TOKEN_TRANSFERS.block_hash).
params.metric: transfer_row_count = COUNT(*) -- count of token transfer events (safe at the transfer grain: one row per transaction_hash+log_index) | sum_value_raw = SUM(value) -- sum of raw token 'value' column across the selected transfer rows (note: token decimals NOT normalized; only meaningful when aggregated for a single token or after applying decimals from a token metadata source) | distinct_tokens = COUNT(DISTINCT token_address) -- number of distinct token contracts in the selection | distinct_senders = COUNT(DISTINCT from_address) -- number of distinct from addresses in the selection | distinct_receivers = COUNT(DISTINCT to_address) -- number of distinct to addresses in the selection
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to ethereum_transactions_base on transaction_hash — safe because this view is one-row-per-transfer; joining to transactions (one transaction row per transaction_hash) will not duplicate transfer-level measures (each transfer may match exactly one transaction row). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to band_blocks_base on block_number or block_hash — safe because blocks are one-row-per-block; joining block-level dimensions will not multiply transfer rows or their measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to ethereum_contracts_latest on token_address = contract_address — safe if ethereum_contracts_latest is one-row-per-contract (latest) because each transfer's token_address maps to at most one contract row, so measures at the transfer grain are preserved. | do NOT join without re-aggregation to any one-to-many view/table relative to the transfer grain (for example, joining to a hypothetically multi-row-per-transaction table such as transaction logs with multiple entries per (transaction_hash, log_index) or to a events table that contains multiple related records per transfer) because that would duplicate transfer rows and inflate measures like transfer_row_count or sum_value_raw. | when joining to reshaped exploded address outputs (e.g., bitcoin_outputs_address_exploded or bitcoin_inputs_address_exploded) or to band_messages_variant_expanded, verify their grain: if the other view is many-rows-per-transaction or many-rows-per-address, you must either (a) aggregate the other side to the transfer grain keys (transaction_hash+log_index or token_address) before joining, or (b) perform the join and then re-aggregate SUM(value) / COUNT(*) etc. on the transfer key to avoid double-counting. | example safe pattern: to get per-transaction token transfer counts, aggregate transfers to transaction_hash (SELECT transaction_hash, COUNT(*) AS transfers_per_tx FROM ethereum_token_transfers_base GROUP BY transaction_hash) and then join to ethereum_transactions_base on transaction_hash. | example unsafe pattern: joining ethereum_token_transfers_base directly to a multi-row-per-transaction table without aggregation — this will multiply transfer records and overcount sums/counts.

views.description: Clean projection of CRYPTO.CRYPTO_ETHEREUM.TOKEN_TRANSFERS with preserved token and log identifiers for token flow analysis. | Use for: token flow between addresses; token transfer volumes over time; join token transfers to transactions/logs

views.name: ethereum_contracts_latest
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  "address" AS address,
  "bytecode" AS bytecode,
  "function_sighashes" AS function_sighashes,
  "is_erc20" AS is_erc20,
  "is_erc721" AS is_erc721,
  "block_timestamp" AS block_timestamp,
  "block_number" AS block_number,
  "block_hash" AS block_hash,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
    PARTITION BY "address"
    ORDER BY "block_number" DESC, "block_timestamp" DESC NULLS LAST
  ) AS address_row_rank
FROM CRYPTO.CRYPTO_ETHEREUM.CONTRACTS
grain: one row per contract address observation (rank exposes latest)

params.description: Provides the latest observed row per Ethereum contract address (latest by block_number then block_timestamp), exposing contract metadata and classification flags.
params.when_to_use: Find the most-recent observed bytecode or metadata for a given contract address. | List contracts with their latest ERC-20 / ERC-721 detection flags. | Filter or join on contracts using their latest block number or timestamp. | Compose analyses that need one-row-per-contract (latest observation) as a stable starting point before joining to activity tables (transactions, token transfers, etc.).
params.output_schema: address: the contract address (derived from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_ETHEREUM.CONTRACTS.address) | bytecode: the on-chain bytecode observed for the contract (derived from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_ETHEREUM.CONTRACTS.bytecode) | function_sighashes: collection/list of function signature hashes detected in the contract bytecode (derived from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_ETHEREUM.CONTRACTS.function_sighashes) | is_erc20: boolean/flag indicating whether the contract was classified as an ERC-20 token (derived from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_ETHEREUM.CONTRACTS.is_erc20) | is_erc721: boolean/flag indicating whether the contract was classified as an ERC-721 token (derived from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_ETHEREUM.CONTRACTS.is_erc721) | block_timestamp: timestamp of the block when this contract row was observed (derived from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_ETHEREUM.CONTRACTS.block_timestamp) | block_number: block number when this contract row was observed (derived from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_ETHEREUM.CONTRACTS.block_number) | block_hash: block hash when this contract row was observed (derived from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_ETHEREUM.CONTRACTS.block_hash) | address_row_rank: integer rank (ROW_NUMBER) partitioned by address ordering rows by block_number desc, block_timestamp desc nulls last; value = 1 indicates the latest-observed row for that address (derived from ROW_NUMBER() over CRYPTO.CRYPTO_ETHEREUM.CONTRACTS partitioned by address)
params.metric: address_row_rank = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY CRYPTO.CRYPTO_ETHEREUM.CONTRACTS.address ORDER BY CRYPTO.CRYPTO_ETHEREUM.CONTRACTS.block_number DESC, CRYPTO.CRYPTO_ETHEREUM.CONTRACTS.block_timestamp DESC NULLS LAST) | latest_row_flag(address) = (address_row_rank = 1)  -- use this predicate to restrict to the latest observation per address
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension or one-row-per-address views/tables on address — safe because this view is one-row-per-address when restricted to address_row_rank = 1, so measures/flags are not duplicated. Example: JOIN ethereum_contracts_latest l ON l.address = some_contracts.address AND l.address_row_rank = 1 | You may safely join on block references (block_number, block_hash) to a one-row-per-block view (e.g., band_blocks_base) on block_number or block_hash — safe because band_blocks_base is one-row-per-block, and ethereum_contracts_latest (when limited to address_row_rank = 1) is one-row-per-address, so the join preserves cardinality (one-to-one or many-contracts-to-one-block). | Do NOT directly join ethereum_contracts_latest (without filtering to address_row_rank = 1) to a one-to-many activity table such as ethereum_token_transfers_base or ethereum_transactions_base expecting measures to remain single-row: if you join the full base (which contains multiple rows per address), you will duplicate contract observations. Always restrict to latest rows first: SELECT ... FROM ethereum_contracts_latest l WHERE l.address_row_rank = 1 JOIN ethereum_token_transfers_base t ON t.token_address = l.address — after filtering to address_row_rank = 1 this join is many-transfers-to-one-contract and does not duplicate the contract's single latest row. | Do NOT join to inherently one-to-many tables (ethereum_transactions_base, ethereum_token_transfers_base, band_messages_variant_expanded, bitcoin_inputs_address_exploded, bitcoin_outputs_address_exploded) unless you intend to aggregate the joined side. If you need aggregated metrics from a many-side, pre-aggregate the many-side (e.g., COUNT(*) or SUM(value) grouped by address) then join the aggregated result to ethereum_contracts_latest (filtered to address_row_rank = 1) to keep measures correct. | If composing further windowing or ranking, preserve the partitioning key 'address' semantics: this view's ranking defines the latest by (block_number desc, block_timestamp desc) — if you re-rank differently, be explicit about the new ordering to avoid mixing historical vs latest observations.

views.description: Latest observed contract metadata per address from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_ETHEREUM.CONTRACTS using block_number ordering. Useful to get most-recent contract attributes (is_erc20/is_erc721/bytecode) for downstream joins. | Use for: get latest contract classification for token analytics; join latest contract metadata to token transfers or transactions

views.name: band_oracle_requests_base
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  "oracle_request_id" AS oracle_request_id,
  "block_height" AS block_height,
  TRY_TO_TIMESTAMP_NTZ("block_timestamp") AS block_timestamp_ts,
  "block_timestamp_truncated" AS block_timestamp_truncated,
  "request" AS request_variant,
  "reports" AS reports_variant,
  "result" AS result_variant,
  "decoded_result" AS decoded_result_variant,
  "oracle_script" AS oracle_script_variant
FROM CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.ORACLE_REQUESTS

params.description: Provides one row per Band oracle request with its identifiers, block timing, and several JSON/variant payload columns (request, reports, result, decoded_result, oracle_script).
params.when_to_use: Fetch details for a specific oracle_request_id (metadata and raw/decoded payloads). | Filter or slice oracle requests by block_height or block_timestamp (time-based analyses). | Compose higher-level aggregates that count or group oracle requests by block, request_variant content, result_variant content, or oracle_script_variant. | Join to block-, transaction-, or message-level views on block_height or oracle_request_id to enrich requests with block/tx context (see composition rules). | Use as a denormalized starting point when you need the raw variant payloads (request/reports/result/decoded_result/oracle_script) for downstream parsing or reshaping.
params.output_schema: oracle_request_id: unique identifier for the oracle request; sourced from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.ORACLE_REQUESTS.oracle_request_id | block_height: block height in which the oracle request was included; sourced from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.ORACLE_REQUESTS.block_height | block_timestamp_ts: block timestamp converted to a TIMESTAMP (NTZ) type using TRY_TO_TIMESTAMP_NTZ; derived from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.ORACLE_REQUESTS.block_timestamp via TRY_TO_TIMESTAMP_NTZ("block_timestamp") | block_timestamp_truncated: precomputed/truncated block timestamp value (string or numeric as present in source); sourced from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.ORACLE_REQUESTS.block_timestamp_truncated | request_variant: raw request payload stored as a VARIANT/JSON; sourced from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.ORACLE_REQUESTS.request | reports_variant: reports payload (VARIANT/JSON) containing reporter submissions; sourced from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.ORACLE_REQUESTS.reports | result_variant: raw result payload as stored (VARIANT/JSON); sourced from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.ORACLE_REQUESTS.result | decoded_result_variant: decoded result payload (VARIANT/JSON) when available; sourced from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.ORACLE_REQUESTS.decoded_result | oracle_script_variant: oracle script definition/payload (VARIANT/JSON); sourced from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.ORACLE_REQUESTS.oracle_script
params.metric: row_identity = oracle_request_id  -- the view is at grain: one row per oracle_request_id | block_timestamp_ts = TRY_TO_TIMESTAMP_NTZ(block_timestamp)  -- conversion expression applied to the source column | no aggregations present in this view (base-level/detail rows). Any count/sum must be computed by the consumer, e.g., total_requests = COUNT(oracle_request_id)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to band_blocks_base on block_height — safe because this view is one-row-per oracle_request_id and band_blocks_base is one-row-per block_height; joining on block_height will not duplicate oracle_request-level rows (each oracle_request has a single block_height). Example: FROM band_oracle_requests_base r JOIN band_blocks_base b ON r.block_height = b.block_height | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to band_transactions_base or band_messages_variant_expanded only when you can join on a unique oracle_request_id present in those views (if those sibling views expose oracle_request_id as unique). If those sibling views are one-row-per-transaction or one-row-per-message and there is exactly one transaction/message per oracle_request_id, the join is safe. Verify uniqueness in the target view before joining. | do NOT join without aggregation to one-to-many children such as a transactions/messages view that contains multiple rows per oracle_request_id (e.g., multiple messages or transfers relating to the same oracle request) because that will multiply this view's rows/measures. Instead either: | - aggregate the child first (e.g., SELECT oracle_request_id, COUNT(*) AS tx_count FROM child GROUP BY oracle_request_id) and then JOIN on oracle_request_id, or | - use a DISTINCT/ROW_NUMBER-based dedupe to reduce the child to one row per oracle_request_id before joining. | do NOT join this view to any exploded/reshaped tables (like *_exploded or variant-expanded sibling views) that produce multiple rows per oracle_request_id unless you intend to expand request-level rows into those multiple rows; if your goal is to preserve metrics cardinality, aggregate the exploded data to one row per oracle_request_id before joining. | when composing aggregates that include counts or sums over requests (e.g., requests per block, per oracle_script), compute them from this view directly: GROUP BY block_height or oracle_script_variant using COUNT(oracle_request_id) to avoid duplication. | nullable/try-conversion note: block_timestamp_ts is produced with TRY_TO_TIMESTAMP_NTZ(block_timestamp) — it can be NULL if conversion fails; account for NULLs in time-based joins/filters.

views.description: Projection of CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.ORACLE_REQUESTS preserving request/decoded_result/report VARIANTs together with block context for oracle analysis. | Use for: analyze oracle request frequency and results; extract specific fields from decoded_result_variant or reports_variant; join oracle requests to blocks/time windows
